hero.title: Frequently asked questions about chair rental
hero.subtitle: Everything about chair rental, prices, legal questions and how ChairMatch works.

q1.q: What is chair rental in the beauty industry?
q1.a: Chair rental (also known as chair rent or booth rental) is a business model in which salon owners rent individual workstations to self-employed beauty professionals. The renter brings their own clients, sets their own prices and pays the salon owner a fixed rent — by the day, by the week or by the month. The model has been established in the US and UK for decades and is growing rapidly in Germany.

q2.q: Is chair rental legal in Germany?
q2.a: Yes, chair rental is legal in Germany. What matters is getting the setup right: the renter must genuinely work independently — own clients, own prices, own entrepreneurial risk. Bogus self-employment must be avoided. ChairMatch provides legally reviewed model contracts.

q3.q: How does chair rental differ from being employed?
q3.a: With chair rental you are self-employed: you set your own hours and prices, keep 100% of your income and carry your own entrepreneurial risk. As an employee you work under the salon’s direction and receive a fixed salary. The biggest difference: as a chair renter you are your own boss.

q4.q: What does chair rental cost in Germany?
q4.a: Costs vary by city and by fit-out. As a guide: €30–60 per day, €150–250 per week, €500–900 per month. In large cities such as Munich or Frankfurt prices sit at the upper end, in smaller cities they are lower. Compared with running your own salon (€2,000–5,000 per month in fixed costs), chair rental is considerably cheaper.

q5.a: Listing a salon on ChairMatch is free. There is no basic fee and no contractual commitment. ChairMatch only charges a small placement fee when a rental is successful. From every booking, €1 goes to children and families in need.

q6.q: What's included in the chair rent?
q6.a: Depending on the salon, chair rent covers: a workstation with chair and mirror, access to a wash station, electricity and water, reception area, waiting area and washrooms. Some salons also offer Wi-Fi, towels and product storage. You will find the exact fit-out in each listing.

q7.q: What taxes apply to chair rental?
q7.a: For the salon owner: rental income is subject to VAT (19%) unless you use the small-business scheme. The income is taxed as commercial income. For the renter: you pay tax on your income from self-employment and can deduct the chair rent as a business expense.

q8.q: Can I rent out chairs while still working myself?
q8.a: Yes, that is the normal case. Most salon owners only rent out the chairs their own team does not use — whether that is an empty spot on certain days or permanently free capacity. That turns dead costs into passive income.

q9.q: How quickly will I find a renter?
q9.a: In popular cities such as Frankfurt, Berlin or Munich we usually place a first renter within 24 to 72 hours. In smaller cities it can take a little longer. The more complete your profile (photos, fit-out, prices), the faster the placement.

q10.q: What happens if the workstation is damaged?
q10.a: Every rental arranged through ChairMatch is insured. Should damage occur, we handle the process. Salon owners carry no financial risk from renting out through our platform.

q11.q: Do I need a trade licence to rent a chair?
q11.a: Yes. As a self-employed beauty professional you need a trade licence (Gewerbeschein). For hairdressers, many German states require a master craftsman certificate (exceptions are possible). Different rules apply to cosmetics, nails and massage — ChairMatch is happy to advise you on the requirements in your region.

q12.q: What insurance do I need as a chair renter?
q12.a: As a self-employed beauty professional we recommend: professional indemnity insurance, public liability insurance and, if applicable, contents insurance for your own equipment. Chair rentals booked through ChairMatch are additionally covered by a platform insurance policy.

q13.q: Can I bring my own products and equipment?
q13.a: Yes, as a chair renter you can generally bring and use your own products and equipment. You will find the exact rules in each salon’s description, or you can agree them directly with the salon owner.

q14.q: Is there a minimum rental period?
q14.a: No. You can rent a chair by the day, by the week or by the month. There are no minimum terms and no notice periods — you can stop or switch salons at any time.

q15.q: Which cities is ChairMatch available in?
q15.a: ChairMatch is available across Germany, with a particular focus on: Frankfurt (incl. Offenbach, Wiesbaden, Darmstadt, Mainz, Hanau), Berlin (incl. Potsdam), Hamburg (incl. Lüneburg), Munich (incl. Augsburg, Nuremberg), Cologne (incl. Bonn, Leverkusen), Düsseldorf (incl. Essen, Duisburg, Wuppertal, Dortmund). New cities are added continuously.

q16.q: How does ChairMatch differ from classified ad sites?
q16.a: ChairMatch specialises in the beauty industry: verified profiles, insurance cover, legally reviewed model contracts and personal support. On classified ad sites you are on your own — without protection and without industry-specific features.
